candidates.explanation: The user appears to be saved with the wrong provider. The snippet is truncated, so the final usersRepository.create({...}) call is not visible. Email registration passes no provider, so this call must default it to AuthProvidersEnum.email. The 422 'needLoginViaProvider:google' means the stored provider is google, which points to a wrong fallback such as `createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.google`. AuthService.validateLogin then sees user.provider !== email and rejects the login.

register spreads the DTO into usersService.create and never sets provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email. It relies entirely on the default in UsersService.create. If that default or the entity/DB column default is wrong, every email-registered user gets the wrong provider.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, default the provider to email: `provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`. Optionally also pass `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly in AuthService.register. Check that the entity column default is not google. Fix any users already created with the wrong provider.

candidates.explanation: The user appears to be saved with the wrong provider. The snippet is truncated, so the final usersRepository.create({...}) call is not visible. Email registration passes no provider, so this call must default it to AuthProvidersEnum.email. The 422 'needLoginViaProvider:google' means the stored provider is google, which points to a wrong fallback such as `createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.google`. AuthService.validateLogin then sees user.provider !== email and rejects the login.

register spreads the DTO into usersService.create and never sets provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email. It relies entirely on the default in UsersService.create. If that default or the entity/DB column default is wrong, every email-registered user gets the wrong provider.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, default the provider to email: `provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`. Optionally also pass `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly in AuthService.register. Check that the entity column default is not google. Fix any users already created with the wrong provider.
